works.followup: Freshly inspected Donemus D13128 public preview, PDF pp. 3–4 / printed pp. 1–2. The score is in C. The first movement begins Lento nervoso, quarter note = 36, with a piano introduction and saxophone figures grouped in 7, 3, 6, 5 and 9, frequent accidentals, large changes of dynamics and tempo, and alternation between solo figures and sustained phrasing. The following section is piu mosso, quarter note = 42. These observations describe concert-pitch score notation, not a transposed tenor range. Publisher confirms 2012 and approximately 11 minutes; added composed, publisher and the exact score/part purchase. McGill's April 22, 2025 bachelor's recital program documents all four movements. Sources: https://webshop.donemus.com/action/front/sheetmusic/13128 ; https://www.mcgill.ca/music/files/music/channels/attach/20250422t2030_bmus-tessmer.pdf . Full transposed range, later movements and a work-specific recording remain unverified.

added_purchase: Donemus alto saxophone and piano, D5473 · https://webshop.donemus.com/action/front/sheetmusic/5473

works.followup: Freshly inspected Donemus D5473 public preview, PDF pp. 3–4 / printed pp. 1–2. The alto staff is explicitly transposed. Menacing at quarter note = 62 opens with long notes and sudden dynamics against violent piano chords. The notation includes a flutter-tongue indication, compressed chromatic figures, and rapid alternation among meters including 5/16, 3/16, 4/16, 9/16, 6/16 and 2/4. Much of that changing-meter passage is piano writing while the saxophone rests, so coordination is a central practical consideration. Piano instructions include strings plucked if possible. Added Donemus and the exact score link; preserved composed 1989 and the existing streaming link. YouTube oEmbed confirms The Pizzaconnection - Chiel Meijering on the composer's channel. Sources: https://webshop.donemus.com/action/front/sheetmusic/5473 ; https://www.chielmeijering.com/works/all-works/saxophone/ ; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4CeoiU74TEo . Opening excerpt only; complete range remains unestablished; audio not auditioned.

works.review_note: content/research-review/Review 0071 - Denis Joly - Cantilene et Danse.md
works.followup: Freshly retrieved Scott D. Kallestad's 2005 University of North Texas DMA dissertation, printed pp. 43–44 / PDF pp. 51–52. His performance analysis identifies graceful slow-section lines, fast scales/arpeggios, sixteenth notes at dotted-quarter = 120, and a plus vite ending with a nine-measure optional cut that removes nearly all that section's sixteenths. Duration approximately 4:30 is his estimate. Appendix printed p. 87 lists the work on three college lists and labels it freshman; this is external evidence, not a SaxoBrain assignment. Hal Leonard/Alphonse Leduc reconfirms AL20698 and eight pages. Its online meter text contains an apparent typo, so the dissertation's account is used for the fast tempo. Added a verified Spotify track by Sandra Leonie Ritter and Chiaki Ohara (4:23). Sources: https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc4959/m2/1/high_res_d/dissertation.pdf ; https://www.halleonard.com/product/48181294/cantilene-et-danse-alto-saxophone-and-piano ; https://open.spotify.com/track/2bnxLad3OlZOpyTLLN6pIb . No actual score notation inspected this pass; original composition year remains unverified (1949 is documented as publication); audio not auditioned.

works.review_note: content/research-review/Review 0150 - Henri Rabaud - Solo de Concours.md
works.followup: Freshly verified Hal Leonard's Southern Music entry for Harry Gee's alto saxophone edition, SS748, Level 5, 16 pages. Pentaedre's authored concert note dates the original clarinet work to 1901, now added to composed. The publisher's related orchestral and band editions confirm that Gee made saxophone/piano and ensemble adaptations, with approximately six-minute duration for those ensemble versions. This is a transcription of a Conservatoire competition work. The available evidence does not establish it as a simplified lyrical adaptation for younger players. Sources: https://www.halleonard.com/product/3774409/solo-de-concours ; https://pentaedre.com/en/concerts/musical-works/competition-solo-op-10-clarinet-and-piano ; https://keiserproductions.com/catalog/southern-music/?ic=&sc=&tc=&tid=F939F850-DE53-4E58-8C3E-5CD1652BDAA9 . The publisher's Closer Look endpoint returned no sample; actual Gee saxophone notation, range and a matching recording remain unverified. Clarinet-original technique is not substituted for saxophone-edition evidence.

works.followup: Freshly retrieved the publisher's history and current revised alto/piano product page. The work was commissioned by Cecil Leeson, completed in piano score in 1940, premiered in 1946, and subsequently revised; Tristan Willems incorporated those revisions into the current performance edition. Preserved composed 1940 and current purchases; added Southern Music, Piano, editor information and an explicitly partial recording page. The ORT Music and the Holocaust page embeds the concerto's first movement with Czech National Symphony Orchestra and Tristan Willems. Its prose names Christopher Creviston but its player caption says Christopher Cranston, so that inconsistent soloist credit is not asserted in the new catalog fact. Sources: https://keiserproductions.com/jaromir-weinbergers-alto-saxophone-concerto-reemerges/ ; https://www.halleonard.com/product/298123/alto-saxophone-concerto-revised ; https://holocaustmusic.ort.org/resistance-and-exile/jaromir-weinberger/ . Publisher sample endpoint returned no excerpt; current revised-edition notation, complete range, technical demands and full-concerto recording remain unverified. Audio not auditioned.
